speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the upcoming rollout of ERP 2.0, whether there are considerations to compensate point-to-point drivers on the downtime that is required for installing the new on-board units in their vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will engage the relevant stakeholders closer to the scheduled period.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For every hour of downtime, our taxis and private hire drivers lose an hour of earnings.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry share how long it may take for installation and how the Ministry would plan for the efficient roll-out, minimising wait times, given that there are now over 50,000 taxis and private hire vehicles in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Are there also plans to work with private hire vehicles' rental companies on sharing the burdens with our drivers, by providing lower rentals during the downtime?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We understand the concerns and in fact, that is the reason why we have been engaging the taxi operators as well as the NTA drivers to look at how we can minimise downtime for the taxi drivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Again, that will help to minimise downtime because it will minimise wait time at the workshop.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the private hire cars, which are either leased from the rental companies or they may be individually owned, we will be commencing installation of the OBU later.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we will, in the same vein, engage the relevant stakeholders – whether it is the ride hail operators or the drivers' association – and look at issues, including ways to minimise the downtime for them.
